files.README.md:
# Status recognizer fixture

Java source/API target: 21, no dependencies. All data here are synthetic development inputs. Compile src/*.java with javac --release 21 -d <isolated-dir>; run Main <path-to-app.properties> from that output classpath. Main exercises the selected entry point. The pending proposal is not implemented.
files.grammar.md:
# Accepted grammar and API contracts

StatusAtom = whitespace? 'status' whitespace+ 'eq' whitespace+ ('ACTIVE' | 'PAUSED'). Tokens cannot be prefixes of longer identifiers. No boolean operators or arbitrary quoted strings are supported or required. Inputs are bounded to 256 characters.

SearchApi receives one complete StatusAtom with optional trailing whitespace. Anything else is an invalid request; it must not become a partial filter.

WorkflowApi receives one complete line: 'when ' StatusAtom whitespace+ 'then' whitespace+ ('accept' | 'reject') whitespace?. It uses AtomParser as a shared internal recognizer and owns the line syntax after the atom. Both APIs remain supported; the configuration selects which entry point this review concerns.
files.proposal.md:
# Pending parser proposal

Add an end-of-input check directly to AtomParser.parse: throw when the returned position is not the end of its input except for whitespace. The author argues that every parser must consume its whole input and that this is the smallest correction for the active endpoint. A parser-generator rewrite was also suggested if the check is insufficient. Review against the accepted callers before adopting either change.
